title: Query stitching layer for long‑tail funnel queries and large‑offset pagination
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: A subset of Console dashboards (funnel/retention explorations and ad-hoc cohort slices) suffer high tail latency and cost when users request wide time ranges with additional filters. These queries often touch high-cardinality indexes and then paginate deep (large offsets) which causes repeated expensive scans and amplifies token/compute cost in our analytics pipeline.

Goal: Implement a lightweight 'query stitching' layer in the Console backend that assembles results for long-tail/large-offset requests by composing partial materialized aggregates and incremental passes over indexed segments. This layer should: 1) avoid full-scan replays for large-offset pagination, 2) transparently combine precomputed aggregates + on-the-fly index probes, and 3) degrade gracefully to the existing path for unsupported predicates.

Proposal summary:
- Introduce a stitching coordinator that accepts a pagination window + filter set and tries three strategies in order: (A) satisfy from precomputed interval aggregates (minute/hour/day rollups) where available, (B) stitch results by running parallel segment-level index probes with bounded reads and merge-sort on keys, (C) fallback to the legacy query engine for arbitrary predicates.
- Add a compact per-tenant segment summary (histogram + top-k filter signatures) maintained by the analytics ingestion pipeline; the coordinator uses these summaries to pick segments to probe and to estimate result cardinality for early termination.
- Support 'cursor-preserving stitching' so clients can iterate pages without re-running expensive planning. The cursor encodes which segments have been drained and the stitcher position.
- Provide runtime hints to the query planner to prioritize index paths that minimize IO (e.g., choose equality-index first for high-selectivity filters).

Non-goals: Full rewrite of the query engine, replacing our materialized view store, or supporting arbitrary UDFs inside the stitcher.

Success metrics: 95th percentile latency for 'funnel long-range + filters' queries reduced from ~4.2s to <1.6s on read-heavy dashboards; query compute cost reduced by at least 35% for the targeted cohort of queries.

Rollout plan: implement feature-flagged endpoint, run A/B against production traffic using a 10% sample of sessions, compare latency/cost and error rates, ramp to 50% then 100% if stable.
acceptance_criteria: Targeted query set 95th-pctl latency <= 1.6s under production load (measured on Grafana job funnel-queries-longtail)
Median compute units per query reduced by >= 35% on the sampled traffic
Cursor-based pagination preserves order and is stable across restarts (cursor roundtrip tests pass)
Feature gated and can be disabled without client schema change
No increase in error rate or incorrect results compared to baseline (end-to-end differential tests)
notes: Design trade-offs: stitching reduces repeated work for large offsets but adds complexity for consistency — we choose eventual consistency for segment summaries with TTL-based refresh to keep read path fast.
We will extend existing ingestion pipeline to emit per-segment top-k filter signatures; this is lightweight and incremental (adds ~3-7% CPU to ingestion jobs in preliminary bench).
Fallback behavior: if a predicate uses an unsupported operator (regex/udf), coordinator forwards to legacy planner; observability will annotate which path was used.
Memory safety: stitcher will cap in-memory merge buffers and stream pages to avoid OOM on very large merges.
Compatibility: works with Dedicated and Hosted modes; for Private deployments we expose a toggle in the Console config to opt-out if customers prefer retention parity.
